subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general messages-level internal-warning router, and which categories and destination modes should it support relative to suppressToolErrors and cron.failureDestination?
rationale: The missing capability crosses config shape, shared reply delivery, channel adapters, existing suppression knobs, and cron-owned destinations, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Add opt-in router
options.body: Introduce a default-compatible messages router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices with explicit destinations while keeping current active-channel delivery as the default.

options.title: Extend suppression only
options.body: Broaden existing suppressToolErrors-style controls without adding alternate destinations, reducing scope but leaving observability routing unsolved.

options.title: Keep scoped owners
options.body: Leave warning handling to cron and channel-specific controls and narrow this issue to any missing owner-specific follow-up.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in router
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-compatible messages router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system notices with explicit destinations while keeping current active-channel delivery as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent warning-suppression work makes this the best available owner for deciding how shared routing should interact with channel behavior.
